source: Owner reported an Android browser screen share; exact source app and browser runtime were not independently verified. Source capture and encoded counters were unavailable in the running bundle.
first_frame: A second authenticated browser joined as listener, selected the live share and displayed moving video after about six seconds.
ui_finding: At an approximately 897 CSS px viewer width, the statistics popover was positioned beyond the left viewport edge. The medium-width alignment is corrected in source, pending deployment and visual retest.
sender_finding: No android_web sender sample appeared. Sender reporting was coupled to a conditional channel panel and a visible-page predicate. Source now binds refresh/reporting to the active share state and permits reporting while the page is hidden. A later Android Chrome attempt did not open the system picker, consistent with that browser lacking getDisplayMedia; the earlier source identity needs confirmation before diagnosing its FPS.
limitation: The anonymous dashboard groups the latest client sample by platform and direction. Packet loss is a cumulative counter, not a rate. Without sender capture/encoded FPS and selected transport RTT, the 14-15 FPS receiver result cannot be assigned to capture, encoder, network or decoder. No supported 30/60 FPS profile is claimed.
privacy: Only bounded aggregate metrics and device-class labels are recorded; no account, channel, track, token, stream content or network address is included.
